records.title: Need for statutory framework to control digital addiction in underage children.
details:
Shri Kesridevsinh Jhala:???????? 
 I seek to draw attention of the
Government to a grave silent epidemic sweeping our nation: digital addiction
among underage children. The recent Economic Survey has rightly sounded the
alarm, warning that compulsive screen time is severely fracturing childrens
cognitive capacity, crushing attention spans, and destroying long-term
productivity. Our children are being exposed to highly weaponized algorithms
designed by global tech giants to ensure endless scrolling, leading to severe
mental health crises, sleep deprivation, and depression. More dangerously,
minors are increasingly exposed to deeply harmful online content,
cyberbullying, and predatory networks without any structural shield. The world
is moving rapidly to protect its youth. Australia has enforced a historic law
imposing a strict ban on social media accounts for children under 16, backed by
massive penalties on tech platforms. France has recently passed legislation
banning social media for under-15s alongside complete mobile phone restrictions
in schools. Even within India, states like Andhra Pradesh and Goa have taken
proactive steps, actively evaluating legal frameworks to restrict underage
social media access and introducing legislative measures. 
 Children
cannot be left at the mercy of manipulative design and toxic content. I urge
the Central Government to step in, look at global and state-level models, and
introduce a comprehensive, central statutory framework with strict age-verification
protocols to curb digital addiction and safeguard the future of our nation.
(ENDS)

records.title: Need for strengthening the ban on single-use plastics through integrated infrastructure reuse.
details:
Shri Kesridevsinh Jhala:
I draw the attention of Government to the
serious menace of plastic pollution spreading across our nation. The
uncontrolled infiltration of microplastics into our food, water, air, and soil
is deeply concerning. This crisis impacts our cattle, wildlife, and marine
ecosystems, with over 267 species already affected. This silent threat
jeopardizes our public health, biodiversity, and long-term sustainability.
Under the visionary leadership of Hon?ble Prime, India has taken proactive
strides banning 19 categories of single-use plastics and achieving a recycling
rate well above the global average. Yet, challenges remain as mismanaged waste
continues to impact our landfills and rivers. We must now move toward a
paradigm of Total Integration, where aggressive reduction and innovative reuse
go hand in hand. I urge the Government to mandate Corporate Social
Responsibility contributions from e-commerce and corporate giants for plastic
recovery, while strictly enforcing Extended Producer Responsibility. We must
scale Central Institute of Petrochemicals Engineering & Technology to train
our MSMEs in manufacturing eco-alternatives like bio-bags, creating sustainable
livelihoods. Most importantly, the plastic we cannot eliminate must be
transformed from a liability into a national asset. I propose a mandate to
integrate collected plastic waste into road construction and infrastructure
projects. Plastic-bitumen blends offer superior durability and water
resistance, turning environmental waste into the very foundation of our
highways. Decisive action today will ensure a cleaner, greener, and
plastic-smart India tomorrow.
??????????? (ENDS)

records.title: Demand for Establishment of a branch of Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) in Gujarat.
details:
Shri Kesridevsinh Jhala: I bring attention
of the Government to the remarkable rise and contributions of the Gujarati Film
Industry to Indian cinema. Historically, Gujarati entrepreneurs, producers,
directors and actors have played an essential role in shaping the cinematic
landscape of our country. Thanks to progressive policies of the Gujarat
Government and ongoing technological advancements, the Gujarati film sector has
witnessed rapid growth. From releasing just 10?20 films annually, the industry
now produces over 75 films each year, with annual investments surpassing
₹150 crore. Further, around 125?150 censor certificates are issued
annually for a diverse range of content, including feature films, advertisements,
short films, documentaries and web content. However, at present, Gujarati
producers and preview committee members are compelled to travel to Mumbai and
other locations for CBFC screenings. This results in significant logistical and
financial strain. The establishment of a CBFC branch in Gujaratideally in
Ahmedabad or Gandhinagarwould greatly benefit all stakeholders by ensuring
timely processing,reducing travel costs and easing the burden on the Mumbai
office. Moreover, such a branch could extend its services to contents in
Kutchhi, Sindhi and potentially Rajasthani-Marwadi languages, thereby enhancing
cultural representation from the region. Under the visionary leadership of
Hon?ble Prime Minister, Gujarat has set benchmarks in several sectors, and it is
now poised to lead in cinematic infrastructure as well. I therefore urge the
Government to kindly expedite the process of establishing a branch of CBFC at
Ahmedabad or Gandhinagar at the earliest. 
??????????? (ENDS)

records.title: Need for mandatory registration of electronic and industrial scrap and recycling units to prevent theft.
details:
Shri Kesridevsinh Digvijaysinh Jhala:?????? 
??????????? I bring to the attention of
the Government a matter of growing concern, the rampant theft and illegal trade
of electronic and industrial scrap, which poses serious risks to national
security, environmental safety, and economic integrity. Despite the existence
of e-waste management rules and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)
frameworks under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, many
scrap and recycling units continue to operate without proper registration or
oversight. This has led to theft of valuable industrial components and
infrastructure; unregulated handling of hazardous materials; loss of recyclable
resources to the informal sector and increased risk of data breaches from
improperly discarded electronics
??????????? The E-Waste (Management)
Rules, 2022, effective from April 1, 2023, mandate registration of recyclers
and refurbishers on the CPCB portal. However, enforcement remains weak, and
many units operate outside the formal system.
??????????? I urge the government to make
registration of all electronic and industrial scrap units mandatory under a
centralized digital portal; link registration with GST, PAN, and geo-tagged
facility verification; conduct regular audits and inspections to prevent
illegal operations; and launch awareness campaigns to encourage compliance and
responsible recycling. 
??????????? This step will not only curb
theft and illegal trade but also strengthen India?s circular economy and
environmental governance.
(ENDS)

records.title: Demand for legal recognition and support of living wills in India.
details:
Shri Kesridevsinh Digvijaysinh Jhala: I
rise today to advocate for the legal recognition and support of Living Wills in
India, an issue vital to preserving human dignity and autonomy in healthcare. A
Living Will, or Advance Medical Directive, enables individuals to express their
medical preferences should they become unable to communicate, especially in
cases of terminal illness, coma, or irreversible conditions. The right to
autonomy in healthcare is enshrined in our Constitution. In 2018, the Hon?ble
Supreme Court upheld the legality of passive euthanasia and affirmed the right
to self-determination in end-of-life care. Yet, despite this landmark ruling,
the practical implementation of Living Wills remains limited. This gap leaves
many vulnerable to prolonged suffering through unwanted medical interventions. To
address this, I propose the following:1. Legal Accessibility and Awareness:
Citizens must be empowered to create Living Wills easily, with clear guidelines
and support systems. 2. Healthcare Integration: Hospitals should be mandated to
honor Living Wills, with proper training for medical staff to respect patient
directives. 3. ????? Safeguards and Oversight: A medical board must review
Living Wills to ensure ethical compliance and prevent misuse. 4. ????? Emotional
Relief for Families: Living Wills spare loved ones from making painful
decisions during medical crises. In conclusion, I urge the Government to bring
legislation that supports the creation and enforcement of Living Wills in
India. Let us uphold every citizen?s right to choose dignity and peace at the
end of life.
(ENDS)

records.title: Demand for establishment of a dedicated cadre for Wildlife Veterinary Services.
details:
Shri
Kesridevsinh Digvijaysinh Jhala: I rise to draw attention
of the Government to a matter of urgent national importance which is the urgent
need to establish a dedicated cadre of wildlife veterinary professionals within
the Forest Departments across India. India is home to some of the world?s most
iconic and endangered wildlife species including elephants, tigers, leopards
and rhinos. Yet, despite the increasing frequency of human-wildlife conflict
and the growing need for specialized care in rescue, rehabilitation and disease
management, there is no dedicated cadre of wildlife veterinarians in most
states. Existing veterinarians are often deputed from the Animal Husbandry
Department, leading to a loss of field experience and continuity in wildlife
care. States like Madhya Pradesh have taken progressive steps by creating a
separate cadre for wildlife vets. It is imperative that other states,
especially those with high biodiversity and conflict zones,? follow suit. A
dedicated cadre would ensure:?Timely response to wildlife emergencies and conflict
situations ?Specialized training in tranquilization, rescue and rehabilitation?
Disease surveillance and outbreak prevention in forest ecosystems ?Long-term
conservation through consistent veterinary support. I urge the Government to
take immediate steps to formulate a national policy for the creation of a
Wildlife Veterinary Services Cadre, with appropriate budgetary support and
training infrastructure.
(ENDS)

records.title: Need for Regulation of Private Detective Agencies
details:
Shri
Kesridevsinh Digvijaysinh Jhala: Private detective agencies are on the rise,
catering to needs from personal investigations like infidelity and background
checks to corporate inquiries such as fraud and due diligence. These agencies
offer valuable services, also pose substantial threats to personal identity and
information security. The lack of stringent regulatory framework has aggravated
concerns, leading to potential misuse and abuse of data. The primary threats
posed by agencies are unauthorized access to and misuse of personal
information. Detectives often employ covert methods to gather data, including
surveillance, tracking, and hacking digital devices. If these agencies remain
unregulated, the potential for violations will escalate. They could resort to
illegal surveillance techniques such as wiretapping, hacking and unauthorized
tracking. Lack of oversight means there is no legal recourse for victims of
these activities, leaving them vulnerable and without protection. Moreover, the
information gathered by agencies could be sold or leaked to third parties,
including criminals. In corporate world, competitors could exploit private
detectives to engage in corporate espionage, stealing trade secrets and
intellectual property, indulging in insider trading. Previous government in
2007 proposed a Private Detective Agencies (Regulation) Bill. However, despite
its significance, the Bill was withdrawn, leaving a regulatory vacuum. The
withdrawal has allowed unregulated growth in the sector, with examples of
malpractices. Introducing legislative framework is imperative to ensure these
agencies are bound by law. Provisions such as establishment of a central
regulatory authority, registration, audits, stringent penalties for breaches,
guidelines on permissible investigative methods, rules to prevent the misuse of
collected data. I urge Government to look into it.
(Ends)
